This is nothing new. Decades has the US been working on this kind of stuff. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Soldier_Systems_Center

That shit is expensive. The current helmets that fighter pilots use cost about $100,000, and the new ones cost about $400,000. The Future Combat System was a program that was going to use displays like scouters in DBZ. The soldiers carried a laptop on their back that was connected to other soldiers via a mesh network. Unlike the system for aircraft, they had to carry the computer and power supply, in addition to their normal gear. The system was heavy and expensive so it was cancelled.

This is a pretty good idea and it's been considered before, but even aside from the expense and other technical issues, one of the big problems with giving SWAT teams and infantry all HUDs is that most soldiers are supposed to deal with the immediate situation and they don't have to have access to all that information.

Worse, giving them that extra information has been shown to slow them down and make them less effective because they have to process all the extra information to make decisions and it just doesn't work very well.

The one big exception to this is that you don't have to go very high up the chain of command before you start getting to people who do mostly spend their time making decisions and passing along orders. If you're in command of a platoon or maybe a squad/section, then that's the level where the extra data starts to actually have a benefit.

So if we started issuing these systems to junior officers and senior NCOs, then that might be good, but that's still probably less than ten percent of the people on the ground. If we handed them out to everybody it'd be a huge clusterfuck.
